Three interlinear additions are present: MD- at the top, the singularity condition above des pts doubles, and the contracted parenthesis above est satisfaite. The lower paragraph has nine baseline lines and continues to the lower edge. Two clipped ink fragments occupy separate rows at the far right; lighter pagination 22 is at lower left. The count 25 comprises 9 upper body lines, 1 bound line, 3 insertion lines, 9 lower body lines, 2 clipped marginal rows and 1 pagination line. The isolated two-speck trace near the right side is documented as an inspection, not counted as a textual line. There is no dark head number.

The m/ar run leads to a q with a long descender, then u and an accented final e. The closing ticks follow without a separate s.
There are two short high tick marks at the opening and another pair at the end. They are not angle-shaped guillemets. The lexical differences are recorded separately.

The lower part has a pronounced curved entry, a raised join and a shallow extended body; a separate straight bar lies above it. Root compared this crop with the barred-m form in 147_scan022 B07, which has the same detached bar and shallow curved body. It is not two straight equals strokes, and the upper bar is not accounted for by the blind ou. The literal barred m remains unexpanded.

After the d lower oval and tall loop comes a distinct low e-cup rising to a small peak; the line then continues into a long ending with a downward hook. That extra ending resembles the final s of des pts in the singularity insertion. Des is preferred, while de remains possible because the joining strokes are compressed.

notes: The page continues the description of geometric MD-curves, retaining the written 0-connexe and dimension 1, the added condition excluding marked points from the singular locus, ordinary double points, and infinitesimal rigidity with an inserted contracted qualification. It excludes the displayed smooth genus-1 case with the indicated empty marking condition and requires the genus-0 irreducible components to have the quoted poids marqué at least 3. The lower paragraph contrasts varying geometric fibre types with an unchanged numerical pair (g,ν), citing the written χ expression and cardinality of the marking object. These are reports of the manuscript statements, not independent mathematical checks. The raised word is retained as autismes|conditions; any proposed expansion of the first candidate appears only in the abbreviation list. The four ornate relative-curve X forms were each inspected and distinguished from the plain crossed hatted X in the lower expression. Root reported the same ornate form on 147_scan022, but reader A did not inspect that page and the current decisions rest on the four current crops. The plain I forms in the raised insertion and the empty-marking condition have no extra underline; the first tuple and final card expression do. C's canceled base candidate remains wholly doubtful; H acknowledges the same struck unreadable ink, so no false omission or certainty-only row is created for it. The two right-edge placeholders preserve clipped ink, with the lower deletion state explicitly uncertain. The isolated two-dot trace has no assigned textual role. The geq/geqslant difference and emph/underline encoding of types and numérique are treated as transcription conventions for the same visible signs, not substantive disagreements. Quote ticks are literal and recorded against H's guillemets. Every agreed word and sign was read in the original/native halves; all 18 crops were personally inspected once. No OCR, web research, TeX compilation, proof checking or additional mathematical background was used.

Independent audit: all four curve symbols retain fraktur X after individual checks of their opposed curves and central cross-strokes, consistent with scan022. The first and final I forms have a separate underline; the two middle forms have only an ordinary lower serif. The long-stemmed loop remains phi|varnothing. The heavy et is live over lighter retracing, with no independent cancellation across both letters. Les has an ascending initial stroke; the ts endings of pts meet the p body at the word baseline and are not separately raised. The quoted phrase is poids marqué: the noun has a looped d, not n followed by a crossed t, and the adjective has no separate final s. The sign before sur une base is revised to barred m after comparison with scan022 B07. The canceled base expression and final des/de remain uncertain. Both clipped edge fragments are preserved, with the lower cancellation state unresolved. The complete lower chi expression was reread; no invariance proof was performed.
